findings.title: Interpolation before partitioning bypasses the `$__range` non-splitting guard
findings.body: At line 299 the targets are interpolated before `querySupportsSplitting` is evaluated at line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` (lines 282-288) explicitly rejects expressions containing `$__range`/`${__range}` because splitting would change the range used for that variable. Once `applyTemplateVariables` has replaced `$__range` with its value, `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` no longer finds it, so such queries are classified as splittable and executed as multiple subqueries. This silently disables the existing guard (and makes its comment false). Either evaluate the guard against the original target before interpolation, or, if pre-interpolation is intended to make `$__range` safe, remove the guard/comment and add a regression test.

findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates each target twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates every target here with `applyTemplateVariables(..., request.filters)`, then each shard request is sent through `runSplitQuery`, which interpolates the same targets again at querySplitting.ts:299. The updated test `Interpolates queries before running` now expects five `applyTemplateVariables` calls for a single target, confirming the double pass. Interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: a variable value that itself contains `$...` will be expanded on the second pass, and ad-hoc filters passed in the third argument can be applied twice, potentially changing the query (and adding repeated work per shard). Interpolate once, or add an option so `runSplitQuery` skips interpolation when called from the shard path.
